headline: President Bush created a White House Office of Homeland Security and a Homeland Security Council by executive order in October 2001.
what_it_does: This order set up a new Office of Homeland Security inside the White House. It also created a Homeland Security Council, a group of senior officials meant to advise the President on homeland security. No summary was provided, so the specific powers and duties of these bodies are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that work on domestic security
who_it_affects.how: They would work with the new White House office and council, though the exact coordination rules are not stated in the title.

who_it_affects.group: Senior White House and Cabinet officials
who_it_affects.how: Some would take part in or work with the new Homeland Security Council.
